proposal.title: 1. SSG General Ledger — Agreement, independent ownership and the 1977–78 development schedule
proposal.reason: Replace the former BPI scenario with the author-requested independent SSG General Ledger partnership. Use the confirmed story dates: agreement 1977-07-28, team/development 1977-08-12, vanilla CP/M/CBASIC release 1978-01-15 and joint AION C/General Ledger Aurelia launch on the morning of 1978-06-06. SSG retains application ownership and sales; AION funds bounded porting and later networking work, not an equity investment. Preserve stable legacy record IDs for reference and review continuity; displayed identities and product scope are SSG General Ledger. Exact original GL/runtime revisions and speed ratios remain unverified. See review_evidence/ssg-general-ledger for source distinctions, scope and validation.

before.description: BPI Systems accepts Adam’s $150,000 investment in exchange for a 33% fully diluted interest. The agreement obliges AION Software to provide knowledge and resources to refactor BPI’s existing code into C with a competitive text-mode TUI. Further investment supports ports to future systems and platforms, after which BPI has the right to buy back Adam’s shares. The same agreement covers BPI’s operating independence, distribution, specialist support and authorised training. Logix and the Academy provide distribution, hardware support and training services.

clauses.statement: Adam agrees to subscribe $150,000 of new capital into BPI Systems for development and working capital. BPI accepts the subscription; it is company funding rather than a payment to existing owners.

The accepted investment agreement allocates Adam a 33% fully diluted interest in BPI Systems in exchange for his $150,000 subscription. Existing owners retain the remaining 67%, subject to the agreed later buyback right.
clauses.unit: percent of BPI fully diluted shares

clauses.statement: AION Software must provide the knowledge, engineering resources and development assistance needed to refactor BPI’s current code into C and deliver a competitive TUI with pseudo-window interaction in text mode. BPI retains ownership of its applications and its independent brand and management.

The cooperation includes further investment and engineering work to port the refactored BPI software to future systems and platforms. AION Software supplies the associated technical knowledge and resources. Additional funding amounts, allocation among contributors, target platforms and schedules remain unspecified.

Following the agreed redevelopment and subsequent porting work, BPI Systems may buy back Adam’s shares. This is BPI’s right, not an automatic transfer or a mandatory buyback. The agreement does not specify a price, valuation formula, exercise date or payment schedule.

BPI retained its management, brand, application ownership, licensing and specialist support. AION Software provided engineering assistance and Logix provided distribution and training. Operational cooperation implements the accepted investment and C/TUI redevelopment agreement while preserving BPI’s operating independence.

BPI owned its applications and managed licensing, updates and specialist support. AION Software supplied engineering assistance, while Logix distributed the products and supported the hardware. Dealers handled installation enquiries. Public presentations described this commercial partnership and identified Adam’s accepted investment and the C/TUI redevelopment partnership.

Academy begins BPI-authorised practical courses and direct distribution under a cooperation agreement. Dealers handle first-line installation enquiries, BPI handles software defects and specialist support, and Logix supports hardware. Tuition, setup services and software licences remain separate.

Alex d’Agapeyeff assigns London-based AION Software engineering capacity for the agreed BPI C/TUI redevelopment, documentation, integration and qualification work. From his appointment, Letwin coordinates systems interfaces and tools within his role. BPI retains application ownership and specialist support; this allocation does not presume delivery or extend AION rights in BPI software.

after.title: AION Software–SSG General Ledger porting, distribution and training agreement

party.role: funding and compiler/TUI engineering partner
independent application owner and publisher
platform, distribution and training-channel partner

after.description: AION Software and Structured Systems Group agree a funded adaptation of SSG General Ledger to native Z80 AION C and the Aurelia ROM TUI. SSG continues its original CBASIC product independently. AION funds tools, porting and qualification work to demonstrate its development platform; SSG retains the accounting product and its commercial proceeds. Logix provides the platform and distribution channel, with Academy training after its establishment.

clauses.statement: Port the existing General Ledger work in progress to native Z80 C with Aurelia TUI interaction. Preserve its ledger rules and reporting, adapting implementation and user interaction rather than commissioning a new accounting suite. Receivables, payables, inventory and payroll modules are outside this agreement.

Sign on 28 July 1977; form the joint team and start development on 12 August 1977. SSG independently releases its vanilla CP/M CBASIC General Ledger on 15 January 1978. Release the Aurelia C/TUI edition during the joint AION C IDE morning presentation on 6 June 1978.

AION funds the agreed port, platform integration, qualification and documentation through milestones for a reconciled core, integrated TUI, pilot acceptance and release handover. This is development sponsorship, not an equity subscription or acquisition. SSG sales are not pledged to repay the sponsorship.

SSG retains General Ledger application source, adaptations, branding, licensing, customer relationships and sales proceeds and profits. Adam, AION and Logix receive no equity, accounting-product ownership or application revenue share. There is no share-buyback arrangement.

AION retains its pre-existing compiler, libraries and reusable platform components. SSG receives continuing rights to build, distribute and maintain the supported General Ledger editions using the agreed redistributable runtime components. Confidential source access and demonstration permissions do not transfer application ownership to AION. Reusable tooling and public APIs remain available to competing publishers on the normal developer terms.

SSG supplies its CBASIC source and specifications as available, accounting expertise, representative test data and report baselines. It controls accounting policy, product acceptance, licensing, releases, defects and specialist customer support. Its vanilla CP/M release remains independently managed.

Alex d’Agapeyeff assigns a protected London engineering team for the C port, tuned assembly kernels, TUI integration and test tooling without displacing the TUI, AION C IDE and Abacus teams. Gordon Letwin coordinates toolchain, ABI and DRI interfaces. Supply a stable development compiler and documented C/assembly and TUI contracts for the August start; remaining work on the public IDE concentrates on optimization, testing and product completion.

Match chart-of-accounts handling, journal posting, corrections, periods, balances, control totals and reports against SSG-approved reference cases. Preserve decimal amounts, required range and rounding, including cases exercising the original CBASIC 14-digit arithmetic. Use explicit decimal or suitably wide scaled-integer routines; ordinary binary floating point or 16-bit arithmetic is not a substitute for the financial contract.

Compare the released CBASIC program and C/TUI port on the same named Aurelia hardware, disks and datasets. Match financial results first, then time validation, searches, posting and report preparation separately from disk and printer waits. Report build, configuration, memory and executable sizes. Do not promise a speed multiplier or attribute every interface gain to compilation; measure shared-ROM TUI calls and optimized libraries separately where practical.

SSG maintains application defects, accounting behaviour and specialist support. Dealers handle installation enquiries, Logix supports hardware, and AION supports its compiler and platform interfaces. After its establishment, Logix Computer Academy provides SSG-authorised General Ledger training, setup assistance and distribution under SSG licensing authority; software licences, courses and setup services remain distinct.

Treat subsequent platform and client/server adaptations as separately scoped phases with acceptance and source/build handover. Client/server work demonstrates networking and recovery; it does not turn AION into an accounting-software vendor. No automatic Apple II release, universal portability, statutory payroll coverage or continuing engineering retainer is included.

At each phase completion, deliver source, build scripts, interface documentation, regression data and maintainer training to SSG. End the special application-development assignment after accepted delivery and agreed defect correction; SSG then develops and supports the product independently while ordinary platform support remains available.

before.title: CAP controlling investment, AION Software identity and CEO continuity
before.description: Adam, CAP and its participating shareholders sign a controlling-investment agreement. CAP continues as the operating company and adopts the AION Software name at closing. Signature creates commitments; the separate closing milestone establishes the ownership change and leadership arrangements.

party.role: investor, purchaser and incoming non-executive chairman
CAP operating company, renamed AION Software at closing
continuing CEO, director and participating shareholder
existing shareholders approving the transaction and conveying the agreed shares

clauses.statement: Adam obtains 70% of voting and economic rights immediately after closing through subscription for new shares and purchase of existing shares. No superior-voting share class is created.
clauses.unit: percent of issued shares at closing

clauses.statement: Former CAP shareholders collectively retain 30% immediately after closing. Alex retains a meaningful personal interest within this block, with individual allocations agreed against the verified share register.
clauses.unit: percent of issued shares at closing

clauses.statement: Adam funds a new-share subscription providing development capital and working capital to the company, plus separate consideration paid to selling shareholders. Amounts and the split require the agreed accounts, valuation and investment schedule; neither company funding nor seller consideration is inferred from the ownership percentages.

Closing requires shareholder consent, verified accounts and ownership, intellectual-property rights, existing corporate commitments, and necessary customer or other change-of-control approvals. The parties settle the subscription and purchase documents and record their completion separately from signature.

CAP continues its operating legal entity as AION Software Ltd, subject to registration of the name. The trading transition may use AION Software, formerly CAP. There is no separately founded Danish software company or acquired Danish subsidiary.

Retain headquarters, contract teams and software development in CAP’s London offices. Coordinate through regular engineering visits with AION Labs in Cambridge; co-operation does not merge the companies or their ownership.

Alex d’Agapeyeff continues as CEO and director, with authority over staffing, organisation, existing customer work and new initiatives within the approved business plan. Adam serves as non-executive chairman. The board retains authority over major financing, acquisitions, strategy and CEO appointment; removal without cause carries agreed severance, without guaranteeing tenure regardless of performance.

The five-member board comprises three Adam nominees and two former-CAP shareholder nominees, including Alex. Minority holders receive regular accounts, information rights and proportionate participation rights in later share issues, subject to the agreed employee award.

Preserve existing customer obligations, specialist teams and commercially sound initiatives. No acquisition-driven redundancies are planned. Allocate customer delivery management separately from the product programme and agree retention arrangements for key staff.

Maintain a separately budgeted product programme for the CP/M TUI API, AION C IDE and Abacus, with provision for application-partner engineering and BPI cooperation in 1977. Continuing CAP work and Alex’s initiatives must preserve the programme’s agreed staffing and delivery commitments. BPI obligations arise only under BPI’s separate agreement.

Approve an initial development budget and recruitment plan separately from seller consideration. Plan initially for 15–25 experienced staff, subject to the actual available team and customer commitments; this planning range is not a claim that those staff have already been hired or released from existing contracts. Review capacity, milestones and funding quarterly.

Existing customer and third-party intellectual-property obligations survive. The investment does not grant rights in CP/M or BPI applications. Define delivery, reuse and licensing rights in the separate partner agreements; retain the company’s compiler, application and reusable-component rights as specified there.

Any later employee award must specify its share source, vesting and dilution. The closing percentages exclude ungranted awards; no undisclosed employee pool or automatic percentage protection is created.

participant.role: AION Software CEO committing redevelopment resources

inputs.description: BPI contributes its existing application code and domain knowledge; AION contributes engineering expertise and resources for C and TUI redevelopment. This refers to pre-existing BPI source material, not a completed Aurelia C/TUI edition.

after.title: AION Software and SSG sign General Ledger porting agreement
after.description: AION Software and SSG sign the General Ledger C/TUI porting agreement. Alex d’Agapeyeff commits London engineering capacity; Keith Parsons represents the independent publisher. SSG supplies its existing General Ledger development and accounting expertise while retaining the separate CBASIC release. AION funds the agreed adaptation and qualification, with no equity stake or share of application sales. The Aurelia port will launch with AION C IDE on the morning of 6 June 1978.

inputs.description: SSG brings General Ledger source under development and accounting specifications; this is not yet its January 1978 commercial CBASIC release.
AION Software’s London product programme supplies compiler, TUI and integration engineering capacity.

outcomes.description: Commission the funded General Ledger port, its joint team, acceptance tests and June 1978 release. SSG retains all application ownership and independent commercial operations.

before.title: BPI development and distribution cooperation
before.description: BPI and Adam implement operational cooperation under the consolidated BPI agreement: independent BPI management, brand, application ownership, licences and specialist support; AION engineering assistance and Logix distribution/training. This cooperation implements the accepted $150,000 investment agreement for Adam’s 33% fully diluted interest, including AION’s C/TUI redevelopment work and future-platform cooperation. Date selected for the alternative scenario. The cooperation also provides for later launch qualification, BPI-authorised Academy training and direct sales, with BPI retaining its software, independent licensing and specialist support.

inputs.description: BPI's accepted 15 February investment and C/TUI redevelopment agreement establishes the obligations implemented by this operational cooperation.

outcomes.description: The partners establish arrangements for qualifying independently licensed BPI applications and supporting their launch, dealer preparation and BPI-authorised Logix Computer Academy courses. BPI retains application ownership, licences and specialist support.

The cooperation supports a later programme of BPI-authorised courses and direct sales starting on 16 June 1978, after the NCC premiere. This start is separate from the Academy's March establishment and June 5 five-city public announcement.

after.title: Joint SSG–AION General Ledger team formed; port development starts
after.description: SSG and AION form the porting team and begin work. Alan Cooper leads SSG application design and accounting acceptance; Alex assigns London C/application, assembly-library, TUI and test engineers, with Gordon Letwin coordinating tools and platform interfaces. SSG continues the CBASIC branch. The team baselines the working C compiler, numeric and file formats, ABI and TUI interface, then starts a headless ledger port and automated result comparisons before integrating forms.

inputs.description: The signed agreement authorises funded development and defines ownership and acceptance.

A working development compiler, linker, assembly interoperability and stable interface baseline are available for the port; optimizer tuning and public IDE packaging continue without changing the agreed application contracts.

outcomes.description: The joint team starts implementation with a shared source, build and regression process. Application acceptance remains SSG’s responsibility; platform interface defects are assigned to AION or DRI through Letwin.

before.title: BPI business and accountant pilot programme
before.description: Target 10–15 pilot businesses and several accounting practices; reconcile results against existing records. Validate representative data volumes, disk/RAM budgets, posting, corrections, backup/restore and supported payroll jurisdictions before launch claims. Date selected for the alternative scenario.

inputs.description: The candidate CP/M implementation supplies the application under test; representative business records and resource budgets define the pilot, without presuming every jurisdiction or configuration is accepted.

outcomes.description: Reconcile pilot results and test posting, corrections, backup/restore, resource limits and supported payroll jurisdictions before making launch claims. This qualification activity does not guarantee that every pilot or configuration passes.

after.title: SSG General Ledger business and accountant pilot programme
after.description: Target 10–15 pilot businesses and several accounting practices for the Aurelia C/TUI General Ledger. Reconcile the January CBASIC release and port against identical records, including postings, corrections, period-end totals and reports. Exercise TUI data entry, backup/restore, interruption recovery, disk-full and memory limits. Pilot participation does not itself establish acceptance.

inputs.description: The native C/TUI candidate is the application under test.
The released vanilla CP/M/CBASIC application provides the reference results and comparison baseline.

outcomes.description: Record reconciled financial results, supported resource limits and unresolved defects. Measure responsiveness on the same Aurelia configuration without inferring speed from language alone; approve only configurations that pass recovery and financial checks.

after.title: SSG releases General Ledger for vanilla CP/M
after.description: SSG releases General Ledger written in CBASIC for vanilla CP/M. Its compiled intermediate code runs under the CBASIC runtime interpreter. The original remains available independently while the joint team continues the native C/TUI Aurelia port. Preserve this release as the controlled accounting and performance baseline; no exact numbered application or runtime revision is assigned.

outcomes.description: The original CP/M/CBASIC General Ledger is commercially released under SSG ownership and support.

after.name: SSG General Ledger — vanilla CP/M / CBASIC edition
after.description: SSG’s independently published General Ledger for ordinary 8080/Z80 CP/M systems, released on 15 January 1978. CBASIC compiles source to intermediate code executed by its runtime interpreter; this is not native Z80 compilation. The accounting environment provides 14-digit arithmetic. The exact General Ledger revision, CBASIC compiler revision and runtime revision are unspecified. It needs no Aurelia ROM TUI and remains a separately maintained product and the functional reference for the Aurelia port.

specification.description: SSG publishes, licenses and supports the original CBASIC application.

after.title: SSG General Ledger AION C/TUI port
after.description: Develop and qualify the Aurelia adaptation of SSG’s General Ledger. The existing ledger work supplies the application semantics; AION contributes tools, integration and focused implementation support. The CBASIC release and C/TUI port remain distinct products.

inputs.description: The agreement establishes the port scope and funded responsibilities.

steps.description: Form the joint team and begin development.
Port ledger logic and explicit decimal routines first; use regression fixtures while SSG independently completes its CBASIC release.
SSG releases the vanilla CP/M edition; freeze a copy and its runtime for regression and same-machine comparisons.

Integrate bounded TUI forms, lists, account tables, selection controls and buttons with shared editing, Tab navigation, shortcuts and copy/paste. Link measured assembly kernels and use the ROM TUI through documented bank-safe calls.
Run business and accountant qualification pilots.
Complete reconciled reports, migration checks, error/recovery tests, resource measurements and instructor preparation. Hand over a reproducible release build for the June 6 joint presentation.

outcomes.description: Deliver SSG’s native Z80 C/TUI General Ledger adaptation, source/build material, reconciled regression suite and maintenance documentation for its June 6 release. Qualification records identify supported configurations; SSG retains release and application ownership.

Sign on 28 July 1977; form the joint team and start development on 12 August 1977. SSG independently releases its vanilla CP/M CBASIC General Ledger on 15 January 1978. Release the Aurelia C/TUI edition during the joint AION C IDE morning presentation on 6 June 1978.

AION funds the agreed port, platform integration, qualification and documentation through milestones for a reconciled core, integrated TUI, pilot acceptance and release handover. This is development sponsorship, not an equity subscription or acquisition. SSG sales are not pledged to repay the sponsorship.

SSG retains General Ledger application source, adaptations, branding, licensing, customer relationships and sales proceeds and profits. Adam, AION and Logix receive no equity, accounting-product ownership or application revenue share. There is no share-buyback arrangement.

AION retains its pre-existing compiler, libraries and reusable platform components. SSG receives continuing rights to build, distribute and maintain the supported General Ledger editions using the agreed redistributable runtime components. Confidential source access and demonstration permissions do not transfer application ownership to AION. Reusable tooling and public APIs remain available to competing publishers on the normal developer terms.

SSG supplies its CBASIC source and specifications as available, accounting expertise, representative test data and report baselines. It controls accounting policy, product acceptance, licensing, releases, defects and specialist customer support. Its vanilla CP/M release remains independently managed.

Alex d’Agapeyeff assigns a protected London engineering team for the C port, tuned assembly kernels, TUI integration and test tooling without displacing the TUI, AION C IDE and Abacus teams. Match chart-of-accounts handling, journal posting, corrections, periods, balances, control totals and reports against SSG-approved reference cases. Preserve decimal amounts, required range and rounding, including cases exercising the original CBASIC 14-digit arithmetic. Use explicit decimal or suitably wide scaled-integer routines; ordinary binary floating point or 16-bit arithmetic is not a substitute for the financial contract.

Compare the released CBASIC program and C/TUI port on the same named Aurelia hardware, disks and datasets. Match financial results first, then time validation, searches, posting and report preparation separately from disk and printer waits. Report build, configuration, memory and executable sizes. Do not promise a speed multiplier or attribute every interface gain to compilation; measure shared-ROM TUI calls and optimized libraries separately where practical.

SSG maintains application defects, accounting behaviour and specialist support. Dealers handle installation enquiries, Logix supports hardware, and AION supports its compiler and platform interfaces. After its establishment, Logix Computer Academy provides SSG-authorised General Ledger training, setup assistance and distribution under SSG licensing authority; software licences, courses and setup services remain distinct.

Treat subsequent platform and client/server adaptations as separately scoped phases with acceptance and source/build handover. Client/server work demonstrates networking and recovery; it does not turn AION into an accounting-software vendor. No automatic Apple II release, universal portability, statutory payroll coverage or continuing engineering retainer is included.

At each phase completion, deliver source, build scripts, interface documentation, regression data and maintainer training to SSG. End the special application-development assignment after accepted delivery and agreed defect correction; SSG then develops and supports the product independently while ordinary platform support remains available.
